subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool routing surface now, or require a broader federation identity/scope contract before any core cross-gateway messaging lands?
rationale: This PR changes who can send messages and spawn runs across Gateway trust boundaries, and the safe URL/auth/session-state contract is a maintainer product and security decision rather than a mechanical patch choice.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this PR paused and require a peer identity, URL policy, operator-scope, idempotency, and session-history contract before implementation proceeds.

options.title: Sponsor narrow peers now
options.body: Explicitly accept the config-gated `gateway.peers` direction and require this PR or a replacement to repair correctness, conflict, docs, and live-proof gaps before merge.

options.title: Replace the branch
options.body: Close or supersede this stale branch after preserving the canonical issue context, then ask for a fresh PR once maintainers choose the direction.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR paused and require a peer identity, URL policy, operator-scope, idempotency, and session-history contract before implementation proceeds.

likelyOwner.reason: The central blocker overlaps the gateway URL security restriction and `sessions_spawn` surface he introduced or hardened.
